features.name: Expression graphing
steps: Open a blank graph
Enter y=x^2-4x+3
Verify that the corresponding parabola is drawn on the right immediately
Change the expression to y=(x-2)^2-1
Verify that the graph updates in real time
Delete that expression
Verify that the curve disappears while the current coordinate viewport remains usable
features.expected: After entering an expression the corresponding curve must be drawn on the right immediately; after modifying the expression the graph updates in real time; after deletion the curve disappears while the coordinate viewport remains usable.

features.name: Multiple expressions linked together
steps: Create three expressions in turn: y=x^2, y=2x+3, x^2+y^2=25
Verify that all three graphs exist at the same time
Temporarily hide one of the expressions without deleting it
Show it again
Delete another expression
Verify that the remaining expressions and the current viewport state are preserved
features.expected: The three expression graphs must all exist at the same time; hiding/showing one does not affect the others; after deleting one, the remaining expressions and the viewport state are preserved.

features.name: Implicit equation graphing
steps: Enter xy=1
Verify that both branches of the hyperbola are drawn
Change it to x=y^2
Verify that the graph becomes a horizontal parabola
Then add x=3y^2
Compare the two curves at the same time
Keep both expressions and verify that the graph relationships are correct
features.expected: An implicit equation must be drawn with the correct shape (both branches of the hyperbola); after modification the graph changes in sync; when the two curves coexist the relationship is correct.

features.name: Parameter sliders
steps: Enter y=ax^2+b
Create sliders for a and b
Modify two parameter values
Verify that the graph changes in real time with the parameters
Set the slider minimum, maximum, and step
Adjust the parameters again
Verify that all dependent variables update correctly according to the new slider configuration
features.expected: Parameter sliders must drive the graph in real time; after setting the minimum/maximum/step, adjusting the parameter updates correctly according to the new configuration.

features.name: Shared parameters linked across expressions
steps: Create a slider for the variable a
Add y=ax, y=ax+2, y=a(x-2)
Modify a several times
Verify that the three curves change in sync
Hide one of the expressions
Modify a again
Restore the hidden expression
Verify that it uses the current latest parameter values
features.expected: When a shared parameter changes all referencing curves must update in sync; after a hidden expression is restored it uses the latest parameter values.

features.name: Custom functions and reuse
steps: Define f(x)=x^2-2x-3
Plot y=f(x)
Add y=f(x-2)+3
Compute a specific value such as f(4)
Modify the original function definition
Verify that all graphs and numeric results referencing f are recomputed at the same time
features.expected: Once a custom function is referenced, modifying the function definition must make all referencing graphs and numeric results recompute in sync.

features.name: Domain / range restrictions
steps: Create y=x^2
Add a domain restriction such as {-2≤x≤3} to an expression
Add another expression with a different restriction
Modify the restriction boundary
Verify that only the curve inside the allowed interval changes
Remove the restriction
Verify that the full curve is restored
features.expected: A domain restriction must affect only the curve inside the restricted interval; after changing the boundary it changes correctly; after removing the restriction the full curve is restored.

features.name: Table → scatter plot
steps: Add a table
Enter several groups of (x,y) data
Verify that the corresponding data points are generated in the graph
Add more rows
Modify an existing numeric value
Verify that the corresponding point's position moves
Adjust the display mode of points or connecting lines
Keep all table data intact during the operations
features.expected: The table data must generate the corresponding scatter points; after modifying values the point positions move; adjusting the display mode does not lose the table data.

features.name: Table → function computation
steps: Define f(x)=x^2+1
Add a table
Enter a set of x values in the first column
Use another column to compute f(x₁) from the first column
Verify that the computation results and the points in the graph are generated correctly
Modify the definition of f(x)
Verify that the table computation results and the graph are recomputed in sync
features.expected: The table computation results and the points in the graph must be generated correctly; after modifying the function definition the table results and the graph are recomputed in sync.

features.name: Data → regression analysis
steps: Create a table and enter one set of sample data
Add a regression expression referencing the table columns
Fit an appropriate model
View the computed regression parameters
Modify one or more source data points
Verify that the regression parameters and the fitted curve are recomputed automatically
Display the original data and the fitted model together
features.expected: The regression must compute the parameters and the fitted curve from the table data; after modifying the source data the parameters and curve are recomputed automatically; the original data and the model are displayed together.

features.name: Statistics and probability
steps: Create a numeric list or table
Compute statistical values such as mean, median, standard deviation, and count
Use a supported probability distribution
Compute or plot PDF / CDF results
Modify the distribution parameters or the source data
Verify that the related values and graphs are recomputed in sync
features.expected: Statistical values and probability-distribution calculations must be correct; after modifying the distribution parameters or the source data the numbers and graphs are recomputed in sync.

features.name: Graph settings
steps: Create several expressions
Open the graph settings
Change the visible X/Y range
Toggle the grid, axis numbering, and minor gridlines
Set the axis labels or step size
Pan and zoom the graph
Use the restore-default-view function
Verify that only the view changes while the expression data stays unchanged
features.expected: The graph settings (range/grid/axes) must take effect; restoring the default view only changes the view while the expression data stays unchanged.

features.name: Expression list organization
steps: Create several expressions
Create a folder and put the related expressions into it
Add a note explaining the model
Collapse and expand the folder
Copy an expression
Modify the copy while keeping the original expression unchanged
Delete the copy
Verify that the other expressions' states are unaffected
features.expected: Folders and notes must correctly organize expressions; after copying, modifying the copy does not affect the original expression; after deleting the copy the other states are unchanged.

features.name: Save → rename → reopen
steps: Build a graph containing several expressions and a custom viewport
Save a graph
Rename
Leave the current graph and open "Saved work"
Find and reopen the graph
Verify that the expressions and graph settings are restored
Duplicate the graph
Modify the copy
Verify that the original graph is unaffected
features.expected: Saving, renaming, and reopening must restore the expressions and graph settings; after duplicating a graph, modifying the copy does not affect the original graph.

features.name: Parametric data models
steps: Create a table containing several groups of observed values
Run a regression on the data
Use the fitted parameters in other expressions
Create another independent parameter slider
Use sliders to construct a second model curve
Compare the regression curve with the parametric curve
Modify the slider and the source data at the same time
Verify that the regression results, derived expressions, and graph always stay consistent
features.expected: After a regression parameter is referenced by other expressions the linkage must be preserved; the parameter/slider model and the regression curve coexist; when the slider or source data changes all results stay consistent.

features.name: Multi-stage mathematical graphs
steps: Define several reusable functions and parameters
Based on these definitions create explicit equations, implicit equations, and expressions with domain restrictions
Adjust the coordinate viewport to show the key intersections
Modify the shared parameter
Verify that all dependent curves are correctly linked
Save a graph
Reopen
Verify that all mathematical state, expression dependencies, and viewport settings are fully restored
features.expected: After saving and reopening, all mathematical state, expression dependencies, and viewport settings must be fully restored.

exclusions.feature:
Desmos Notebook
Do not explore or reproduce Notebook documents, pages, text blocks, embedded calculator blocks, or Notebook publishing
exclusions.reason: It belongs to a separate Desmos product rather than the core features of the 2D graphing calculator at desmos.com/calculator

exclusions.feature:
3D Graphing Calculator
Exclude 3D axes, 3D surfaces, 3D points, view rotation, and 3D camera operations
exclusions.reason: It belongs to the separate 3D Calculator and is outside this benchmark's 2D calculator scope

exclusions.feature:
Geometry tools
Exclude compass-and-straightedge constructions, angle constructions, geometric transformations, and the Geometry-specific toolbar
exclusions.reason: It belongs to a separate geometry product and is outside the core scope of the 2D Graphing Calculator

exclusions.feature:
Classroom / teacher activities
Exclude classroom activities, course creation, the teacher dashboard, student sessions, class codes, assignments, and classroom management
exclusions.reason: Depends on an education platform and multi-user system and is not part of the single-user calculator workflow

exclusions.feature:
Exam / test-mode calculator
Exclude state exam modes, locked mode, exam feature allowlists, and institution-specific restrictions
exclusions.reason: The test-mode calculator is itself a different feature subset and should not be evaluated together with the standard calculator

exclusions.feature:
Real-time multi-user collaboration
Exclude simultaneous editing, real-time cursors, multi-user conflict resolution, and collaboration rooms
exclusions.reason: Depends on real-time collaboration infrastructure and is not suitable as a single-agent web-reproduction benchmark

exclusions.feature:
Account authentication
Exclude registration, login, password recovery, login security, third-party identity authentication, and account security settings
exclusions.reason: It belongs to account infrastructure and is unrelated to mathematical graph interaction

exclusions.feature:
External sharing infrastructure
Exclude email sharing, social sharing, public link permissions, external embed services, and social previews
exclusions.reason: It belongs to content distribution and the permission system, not the calculator's mathematical capabilities

exclusions.feature:
Full version history
Exclude all historical version storage, cross-session rollback, remote revision management, and multi-user version-conflict handling
exclusions.reason: The benchmark only needs the user-visible persistence of save/reopen

exclusions.feature:
Full reproduction of the Desmos cloud backend
Reproducing the real Desmos database, the Saved Work cloud-storage architecture, or the internal sync system is not required
exclusions.reason: The benchmark only concerns user-visible state persistence and does not test the proprietary backend architecture

exclusions.feature:
1:1 compatibility with the full math engine
Full coverage of all undocumented parsing rules, all numerical-precision details, all symbolic-simplification rules, and every advanced function is not required
exclusions.reason: Fully replicating the entire Desmos math engine is too costly and would also deviate from the purpose of an agent-workflow benchmark

exclusions.feature:
Exhaustively cover all statistics functions
cov, spearman, quantile, all statistics helpers, and all statistics edge cases are not tested one by one
exclusions.reason: Only representative end-to-end statistics and probability tasks are needed, and it should not degenerate into atomic function unit tests

exclusions.feature:
Exhaustively cover all math helper functions
lcm, gcd, nCr, nPr, polygon, distance, and the various color-space functions are not benchmarked one by one
exclusions.reason: These are mathematical primitives and not independent agent task threads

exclusions.feature:
The complete statistical-inference suite
Exclude reproducing every z-test, t-test, chi-square test, confidence-interval helper, and all inference object fields one by one
exclusions.reason: Unless a separate statistics benchmark is created, representative statistics tasks are enough

exclusions.feature:
Audio / sound accessibility features
Exclude sonification, pitch mapping, audio graph navigation, sound playback, and exact audio behavior
exclusions.reason: Depends on browser audio and accessibility systems and is weakly related to the visual math workflow

exclusions.feature:
Braille mode
Exclude Braille input/output, hardware Braille displays, and screen-reader-specific math navigation
exclusions.reason: Depends on a special accessibility hardware/software stack

exclusions.feature:
Advanced photo-asset workflows
Exclude the full image-upload system, cloud image storage, image hotspots, remote image management, and image accessibility metadata
exclusions.reason: Images are an auxiliary graphical element and not part of the main mathematical computation chain

exclusions.feature:
Advanced interactive programming such as Ticker / Actions
Exclude the automatic Ticker, Actions, advanced state mutation, and event-driven complex interactive graph programming
exclusions.reason: It is an advanced optional capability that would significantly increase implementation complexity but is not part of the basic calculator core

exclusions.feature:
Pixel-perfect rendering
Anti-aliasing, curve subdivision, fonts, tick positions, grid rendering, and numeric sampling are not required to match Desmos pixel by pixel
exclusions.reason: The benchmark should focus on mathematical structure and interaction results rather than an exact copy of the underlying renderer

exclusions.feature:
Mobile / touch behavior
Exclude phone keyboard layouts, pinch zoom, touch gestures, screen rotation, and native app behavior
exclusions.reason: The benchmark is fixed to desktop web

exclusions.feature:
Example gallery / public graph content library
Reproducing all Desmos example graphs, public works, the search index, and community graph data is not required
exclusions.reason: It is an external content dataset, not the calculator itself

exclusions.feature:
Full multilingual localization
All language translations, all locale number formats, and all regional math-keyboard behaviors are not required
exclusions.reason: The benchmark can fix a single UI language and does not need to build a full internationalization system

exclusions.feature:
Help center / tutorials
Exclude official tutorial videos, help-center search, documentation sites, and customer-support workflows
exclusions.reason: It belongs to a supporting content system and is not a core calculator feature
